## Instructions

This quiz covers Discussion section writing and prepares you for the EDS (Empirical Data Skills) assignment. The EDS requires by-hand calculations and APA reporting.

---

## Part 1: Discussion Section Structure

### Question 1: Discussion Components

A Discussion section typically includes (in order):

First: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Summary of findings (did results support hypothesis?)</option><option value=''>Literature review</option><option value=''>Methodology critique</option><option value=''>Future research</option></select>

Then: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Raw data</option><option value='answer'>Interpretation and relation to previous research</option><option value=''>Participant demographics</option><option value=''>Statistical formulas</option></select>

Then: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>More statistics</option><option value='answer'>Limitations of the study</option><option value=''>Introduction material</option><option value=''>Another hypothesis</option></select>

Finally: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>A new study design</option><option value='answer'>Implications and future directions</option><option value=''>The abstract</option><option value=''>References</option></select>

### Question 2: Discussion vs Results

Which statement belongs in the Discussion, NOT the Results?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>M = 45.30, SD = 8.25</option><option value=''>t(48) = 2.45, p = .018</option><option value='answer'>This finding supports Smith's (2020) theory that...</option><option value=''>The experimental group scored higher than the control group</option></select>

### Question 3: Starting the Discussion

A good opening sentence for the Discussion might be:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>We did a study on memory</option><option value='answer'>The present study examined whether X affects Y. Results supported/did not support the hypothesis that...</option><option value=''>Statistics showed significance</option><option value=''>There were limitations</option></select>

---

## Part 2: Interpreting and Discussing Results

### Question 4: Connecting to Literature

When discussing your findings, you should:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Ignore previous research</option><option value=''>Only cite studies that agree with your findings</option><option value='answer'>Relate findings to previous research, explaining consistency or inconsistency</option><option value=''>Copy the Introduction</option></select>

### Question 5: Discussing Non-Significant Results

If your results are NOT significant, you should:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Hide the study and start again</option><option value=''>Claim significance anyway</option><option value='answer'>Discuss possible reasons (e.g., low power, measurement issues, genuine null effect)</option><option value=''>Only write a short Discussion</option></select>

### Question 6: Causation Claims

In your Discussion, you can claim causation if:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Your p-value is very small</option><option value='answer'>You used an experimental design with random assignment</option><option value=''>You have a large correlation</option><option value=''>Your effect size is large</option></select>

Correlational findings should be discussed as:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Causal relationships</option><option value='answer'>Associations/relationships (not causes)</option><option value=''>Unimportant</option><option value=''>Definitive proof</option></select>

---

## Part 3: Limitations

### Question 7: Common Limitations

Which is a valid limitation to discuss?

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>The study was difficult to conduct</option><option value='answer'>The sample was limited to university students, which may affect generalisability</option><option value=''>I didn't like the results</option><option value=''>Statistics are confusing</option></select>

### Question 8: Constructive Limitations

Good limitations are:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Vague complaints about the study</option><option value='answer'>Specific issues that could have affected results, with suggestions for improvement</option><option value=''>Excuses for non-significant results</option><option value=''>Comments about how hard you worked</option></select>

### Question 9: Limitation Examples

Match the limitation to its category:

"Only students were sampled" → <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Sample/generalisability</option><option value=''>Measurement</option><option value=''>Design</option><option value=''>Statistical</option></select>

"Self-report measures may not reflect actual behaviour" → <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Sample</option><option value='answer'>Measurement</option><option value=''>Design</option><option value=''>Statistical</option></select>

"Between-subjects design may have allowed individual differences to affect results" → <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Sample</option><option value=''>Measurement</option><option value='answer'>Design</option><option value=''>Statistical</option></select>

---

## Part 4: EDS Preparation - By-Hand Calculations

### Question 10: Calculating the Mean

Calculate the mean of: 8, 12, 15, 9, 11

Sum = <input class='webex-solveme nospaces ignorecase' size='2' data-answer='["55"]'/>

N = <input class='webex-solveme nospaces ignorecase' size='1' data-answer='["5"]'/>

Mean = <input class='webex-solveme nospaces ignorecase' size='2' data-answer='["11"]'/>

### Question 11: Calculating Standard Deviation

For the data: 10, 12, 14 (Mean = 12)

Step 1: Deviations from mean are: -2, 0, +2

Step 2: Squared deviations: 4, 0, 4

Step 3: Sum of squared deviations = <input class='webex-solveme nospaces ignorecase' size='1' data-answer='["8"]'/>

Step 4: Divide by (N-1) = 8/2 = <input class='webex-solveme nospaces ignorecase' size='1' data-answer='["4"]'/> ← This is the variance

Step 5: SD = √4 = <input class='webex-solveme nospaces ignorecase' size='1' data-answer='["2"]'/>

### Question 12: By-Hand t-Test Concept

The t-statistic formula is:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Difference between means divided by standard error</option><option value=''>Mean divided by standard deviation</option><option value=''>Sum of scores divided by N</option><option value=''>Variance times sample size</option></select>

A larger t-value (further from 0) indicates:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>A smaller effect</option><option value='answer'>A larger difference relative to variability</option><option value=''>An error</option><option value=''>Non-significance</option></select>

---

## Part 5: EDS-Style Questions

::: {.webex-check .webex-box}

### EDS Practice 1

A researcher compares reaction times between participants who had coffee (n=10, M=250ms, SD=30) versus no coffee (n=10, M=280ms, SD=35).

1. **What is the IV?** <input class='webex-solveme nospaces ignorecase' size='16' data-answer='["coffee","caffeine","drink","coffee condition"]'/>

2. **What is the DV?** <input class='webex-solveme nospaces ignorecase' size='13' data-answer='["reaction time","RT"]'/>

3. **What type of design is this?** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Between-subjects</option><option value=''>Within-subjects</option><option value=''>Correlational</option><option value=''>Matched pairs</option></select>

4. **What test would you use?** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Independent t-test</option><option value=''>Paired t-test</option><option value=''>Pearson's r</option><option value=''>Chi-square</option></select>

5. **Is the DV continuous, discrete, or categorical?** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Continuous</option><option value=''>Discrete</option><option value=''>Categorical</option><option value=''>Ordinal</option></select>

:::

::: {.webex-check .webex-box}

### EDS Practice 2: Reporting Results

Given these results: t(18) = 2.45, p = .025, d = 0.73

Write the APA-formatted report by filling in the blanks:

"An independent samples t-test revealed a significant difference in reaction times between the coffee group (*M* = 250.00, *SD* = 30.00) and no-coffee group (*M* = 280.00, *SD* = 35.00), *t*(<input class='webex-solveme nospaces ignorecase' size='2' data-answer='["18"]'/>) = <input class='webex-solveme nospaces ignorecase' size='4' data-answer='["2.45"]'/>, *p* = <input class='webex-solveme nospaces ignorecase' size='5' data-answer='[".025","0.025"]'/>, *d* = <input class='webex-solveme nospaces ignorecase' size='4' data-answer='["0.73",".73"]'/>."

Effect size interpretation: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Small</option><option value='answer'>Medium</option><option value=''>Large</option><option value=''>Negligible</option></select>

:::

::: {.webex-check .webex-box}

### EDS Practice 3: Correlation Reporting

A correlation between anxiety and test performance yields: r(38) = -.42, p = .008

1. **Is this significant at α = .05?** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

2. **Direction of relationship:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Positive</option><option value='answer'>Negative</option><option value=''>No relationship</option><option value=''>Perfect</option></select>

3. **Strength:** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Weak</option><option value='answer'>Moderate</option><option value=''>Strong</option><option value=''>Very weak</option></select>

4. **Can we say anxiety CAUSES poor performance?** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>TRUE</option><option value='answer'>FALSE</option></select>

5. **Calculate r²:** <input class='webex-solveme nospaces ignorecase' size='6' data-answer='[".1764","0.1764","17.64%","18%",".18"]'/>

:::

Section A of the EDS requires you to:

Write a hypothesis <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

Identify design, IV, DV, and data type <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

Calculate mean and SD by hand <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

Conduct a by-hand statistical test <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

Write a full lab report <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>TRUE</option><option value='answer'>FALSE</option></select>

Report results in APA format <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

### Question 14: EDS Section B

Section B asks about:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>More statistics</option><option value='answer'>Methodological improvements, individual differences, and ecological validity</option><option value=''>Rewriting Section A</option><option value=''>Planning a new study</option></select>

### Question 15: Ecological Validity

Ecological validity refers to:

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Whether the study is environmentally friendly</option><option value='answer'>Whether findings generalise to real-world settings</option><option value=''>Whether the design is ecological</option><option value=''>The number of participants</option></select>

---

## Summary Checklist

Before the EDS assignment, verify you can:

- [ ] Write a complete Discussion section (summary, interpretation, limitations, future directions)
- [ ] Calculate mean by hand (sum / n)
- [ ] Calculate SD by hand (deviations → squared → sum → divide by n-1 → square root)
- [ ] Understand t-test logic (difference relative to variability)
- [ ] Report all statistics in APA format
- [ ] Identify IV, DV, design type, and data type
- [ ] Explain correlation ≠ causation
- [ ] Discuss ecological validity and individual differences

::: {.callout-important}

Submit your EDS assignment by the deadline. This assessment is worth 20% of your module grade. Show all working for by-hand calculations.
:::
